title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Veneto and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show DOC or DOCG, like Amarone della Valpolicella or Soave Classico, plus Classico for the historic zone, Superiore for higher ripeness or ageing, and Ripasso. For Prosecco, look for Superiore, Rive or Cartizze, and the sweetness: Brut, Extra Dry, which is sweeter than Brut, and Dry.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Valpolicella suits salumi and pasta; Ripasso suits risotto and roasts; Amarone suits braised beef, game and aged cheese, and flavours risotto all'Amarone. Soave suits risotto, seafood and antipasti. Prosecco suits cicchetti, Venetian small bites, and makes the Spritz and the Bellini. Recioto suits pandoro.

steps.prompt: Which cocktail uses Prosecco and white peach?

steps.body: In Venice, a glass of Prosecco with cicchetti at a bàcaro, a small wine bar, is the local way to start an evening.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show Classico, Superiore and Ripasso
Amarone suits braised beef; Soave suits risotto
Prosecco suits cicchetti and makes the Spritz
